original_question: If central simple F-algebras A and B have the same degree and generate the same subgroup of Br(F), must their generic splitting fields F(A) and F(B) be isomorphic? Equivalently, are the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B) necessarily F-birational under that hypothesis?
target_in_paper: Section 10, Conjecture 10.2 (Amitsur's Conjecture), together with the immediately preceding Theorem 10.1(2) and the sentence right after Conjecture 10.2 identifying the Severi-Brauer birational formulation.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It has the correct objects (central simple F-algebras A and B), the correct hypotheses (same degree and same subgroup of Br(F)), the correct conclusion (isomorphism of generic splitting fields), and the correct equivalent reformulation in terms of F-birationality of the associated Severi-Brauer varieties. This is exactly the content of Amitsur's Conjecture as stated in Section 10.
missing_details: State explicitly that Br(F) is the Brauer group of the base field F and that the subgroup condition means the cyclic subgroup generated by the Brauer classes [A] and [B].
Define F(A) and F(B) as the generic splitting fields of A and B; in the paper these are identified with the function fields of the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B).
Specify that the isomorphism F(A) ≅ F(B) is meant as an F-isomorphism of fields.
Make explicit that SB(A) and SB(B) are the Severi-Brauer varieties associated to A and B.
Keep the scope at central simple algebras, not just division algebras; the statement in the paper is formulated for central simple F-algebras.
refined_question: Let F be a field, and let A and B be central simple F-algebras of the same degree. Assume that their Brauer classes [A] and [B] generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(F). If F(A) and F(B) denote the generic splitting fields of A and B (equivalently, the function fields of the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B)), must F(A) and F(B) be F-isomorphic?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if A and B are central simple F-algebras of the same degree and [A],[B] generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(F), must the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B) be F-birational?
justification: The draft is targeting Amitsur's Conjecture in Section 10, not a neighboring problem from another section. Section 10 introduces the generic splitting field F(A) and recalls that it is the function field of the Severi-Brauer variety SB(A). Theorem 10.1(2) states that if F(A) and F(B) are isomorphic, then A and B generate the same subgroup of Br(F). Conjecture 10.2 immediately asks for the converse, with the extra hypothesis that A and B have the same degree. The very next sentence states the equivalent formulation in terms of F-birationality of SB(A) and SB(B). So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is essentially your draft with the notation made explicit and the field-isomorphism interpreted over F.
